newsitem.title: USA: Phila Fed-region's industry growth slower in April.
newsitem.headline: Phila Fed-region's industry growth slower in April.

text.p: Michael Trebing, an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, said regional manufacturing was growing more slowly in April as demand appeared to moderate.
The Philadelphia Fed's business outlook survey fell to 5.7 in April versus 21.1 in March.
"This drop probably reflects some slowing in the growth rate from the previous couple of months," Trebing said in a teleconference.
Both prices paid and prices received indices rose in the latest report, but that was not yet reflected in finals goods prices, the Philadelphia Fed economist said.
"It looks to me as though there are input price pressures but as of yet they haven't shown in final goods prices," Trebing said.
Asked about the region's manufacturing employment situation, Trebing said a majority of firms are still "upbeat" about adding to payrolls in coming months.
While regional manufacturing showed signs of slowing, Trebing cautioned against correlating that with a national slowdown in manufacturing growth.
"It's a regional manufacturing survey and it reflects our region rather than the U.S. economy," he said. "So it's too soon to draw conclusions about what's going on."
